blocks.title: apiVersion and kind
blocks.what: apiVersion names the API that defines this object. kind names the type of object, here a Pod.
blocks.why: Kubernetes reads these two lines first to know which rules apply to the rest.
blocks.ifRemoved: kubectl refuses the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: Part 1: the API version and the kind of object

blocks.title: metadata: who it is
blocks.what: metadata identifies the object. Here it gives the Pod its name, myfirstpod.
blocks.why: You use the name to find, change, or delete the object later.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Pod, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: Part 2: metadata, which names the object
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: myfirstpod

blocks.title: spec: what you want
blocks.what: spec describes what you want. Here it is one container started from the nginx image.
blocks.why: Kubernetes compares spec with what is really running and works to make them match.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Pod, because a Pod needs at least one container.
blocks.comment: Part 3: spec, the state you want
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: myfirstpod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: myfirstcontainer
      image: nginx:1.30.4

blocks.title: The four parts together
blocks.what: The last lines record port 80, where nginx listens. Every line now sits under one of the four parts.
blocks.why: After you apply the file, Kubernetes adds a fifth part, status. It reports what is really happening.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without ports, the Pod runs the same. The list only tells readers which port nginx uses.
blocks.comment: The port nginx listens on, inside spec
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: myfirstpod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: myfirstcontainer
      image: nginx:1.30.4
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80

notes.apiVersion: Part 1: the API that defines this kind. Pods are in the core v1 API.
notes.kind: Part 1: the type of object to create. Here, a Pod.
notes.metadata: Part 2: details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The Pod's name. It must be unique among Pods in the same namespace.
notes.spec: Part 3: the state you want. Kubernetes works to make the cluster match it.
notes.spec.containers: The containers in this Pod. Run kubectl explain pod.spec.containers to see every field.
notes.spec.containers[].name: The container's name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.containers[].image: The image to run, with a fixed version tag, so every run uses the same version.
notes.spec.containers[].ports: Ports the container listens on. This list is mostly informational.
notes.spec.containers[].ports[].containerPort: The port number nginx listens on inside the container.

tryIt.result: Shows your four parts, plus a status section Kubernetes added, such as phase: Running.
